### Lane B — every chip in the bar's machine cluster does one named thing, and Settings reaches Home's garden

`active` · `@legeos.work.bar-cluster-clickable-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

The user's report on the installed session at gfbe4480 was that the bar's bottom-right buttons are not clickable, that network should open nm-tray-2, that the separate power/battery bar should become a full OS Settings button, that date/time should open an existing calendar rather than a new one, and that the furthest bottom-right button was unlabelled and frightening. Finding 6 of the Homegarden usability review adds that Settings excludes every `shell.home-garden.*` key, so default-on automation has no graphical settings.

Three of those were literal: the readings chip and the clock had no click handler at all, so a click on either fell through to the bar's own ground and merely re-activated the window. The fourth was worse than literal: the network chip *was* wired, but `app.rs::network_control_app` resolved the control by desktop-file name (`*nm-tray.desktop`) while the action `network.open-control` has always declared `Requires::Provider(ProviderRole::NetworkStatusUi)`. On this host `lege providers` prints `network-status-ui  no application declares this role` and the registry nonetheless holds `desktop-import.nm-tray.desktop` for Ubuntu's stock nm-tray 0.5.1 — which ignores `--popup`, only ever draws a tray icon, and had no tray to draw into. The chip lit up and launched something invisible.

The work: the cluster becomes account · clock · network · Settings, right to left, with the readings moved into the account popover's first line and their 112 pixels spent on a Settings chip; the account chip wears the account's name beside its mark; the confirm rows read "Click again to log out"; the clock gains `clock.open-calendar`, which resolves the first application declaring `Categories=Calendar` (gsimplecal preferred, and now in the desktop seed); the network chip resolves the provider role and nothing else; and Settings gains a Homegarden tab with the typed `shell.home-garden.*` keys, an editable ignore list and the hidden places from `HomeGarden1.Contexts`, each with an Unhide that calls `Hide(path, false)`.

### Lane C — blooms: an earned Place says what arrived in it, and forgets when you open it

`active` · `@legeos.work.homegarden-blooms-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Phase 5 rewritten on the user's rule that content changes may alter what an earned Place shows but never create, resize, move or promote one. At each tending moment the daemon reads the shared index once through Files.Index1.ChangesSince from a persisted change cursor (never a subscription; SnapshotRequired below the retained floor resets the cursor and shows nothing; a cursor of 0 takes the position and shows nothing), reduces the page to Arrived/Moved/Gone, attributes each through the existing root walk and ignore list, and looks it up against existing contexts of stage Tile or above, never inserting. A Bloom {kind: Arrived, since: GardenMoment, items (8), total (99)} on the context appears as `N new ·` on the state line, as a mark in the body, and in `lege garden why`; it resolves through the file-opened Observe, which the Files app now calls beside Recents; an unanswered bloom drops after five later sessions. A move whose old_path is a context root rewrites the root and keeps material_seed and buckets. Docs: the seven-day Make-this-a-project row and the 30-day mount retention are deleted, the remaining calendar prose and Appendix A are restated in sessions and garden-hours, §5.4's struct and threshold table match the shipped model, the idle_hours JSON key is idle_garden_hours. Not here: media consumption (no media role, VLC is the player, MPRIS cannot give progress without polling); Phase 6 material rendering.

### Lane A — a day at the terminal reaches the garden: the clock accumulates, the hook loads in kitty, Home stops feeding on itself, Desktop is an ordinary pinned Place, and the bar's chips get their icons

`active` · `@legeos.work.homegarden-day-reaches-the-garden-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1` · **at risk**

Fix the four defects the half day exposed (@legeos.observation.homegarden-half-day-grew-only-the-desktop-tray-20260909) so a day of real work registers. (1) GardenClock folds its open interval into active_ms at every persist (a checkpoint), so a session that ends without a lock edge still ages the garden and last-used moments no longer include an unpersisted interval. (2) The terminal prompt hook is delivered through /etc/bash.bashrc by the legeos-cli maintainer scripts, the file a non-login interactive bash reads, with a check that can fail. (3) Drawing an open folder window at its own anchor records nothing; only navigation away from the anchor is directory-opened. (4) The user's decision on open choice (1): the permanent Desktop tray goes; the first run records one placed-on-home for the XDG Desktop directory so it starts pinned; a saved tray tile is migrated away; unpin, hide and recession then apply to it like any Place. Attribution is left as it is: the user chose that a folder of projects may be the Place and the tree beneath it carries the repositories (no VCS-root heuristic). (5) The bar's all-initials chips: the offline resolver finds every icon on this host and the bar reads the key the loader writes, so the two silent failure paths (an identity that fails AppId parsing; a lookup miss never retried) now log; the cause is read from one session's journal. Not here: created-or-renamed from filed, media roles, threshold retuning.

### Lane B — a Place draws the form its use earned: branch, shelf or plain, a lightly used place is a line, and the roles row goes

`active` · `@legeos.work.homegarden-growth-forms-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

First cut of @legeos.decision.a-place-is-a-drawn-structure-not-a-richer-rectangle, simple before beautiful. (1) A headless garden fixture (LEGE_BASELINE_GARDEN=branch|shelf|plain) grows two Places into the baseline field through the real tender, so each form renders and hashes without a compositor. (2) A `form` on each context (Plain, Branch, Shelf, Folio), derived at tending moments by folding the activity tree (directories weighted by depth and by a Terminal or CodeEditor role; leaves classified by extension) with a 2.0 floor, a 1.5x margin and a two-session dwell; only form, form_candidate and form_candidate_since persist, in the free-form Contexts JSON. (3) A forms painter (surface/place_forms.rs), one fn per form: a 2D branch with the Place root as trunk and the used descendants as branches, thicker by share; a shelf of item cells under a rule; plain falls back to the folder body. PLACE_ROLES and the indented branch list are deleted; the place.open-* actions stay in the context menu. Bloomed items are drawn in the accent (post-merge, eed1bc2). (4) The span ladder: Trace 2x1, Tile 2x2, Expanded 4x3, a new top stage Dominant 6x4; the Folder floor is 2x1 and GROWTH_ROOM 6x4. (5) A warm mineral substrate. Deferred: the folio drawing, shelf thumbnails, and any stylised vector or fractal tree, which is the later pass the user asked for.

### Homegarden Phases 0–3: the activity ledger and Garden Clock, the tender, tending at reveal and session start, and the rung-aware Place tile

`active` · `@legeos.work.homegarden-phases-0-3/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Build the Homegarden model far enough to judge it in a day's use (@legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places, docs/garden/*.md): (1) a pure ledger in lege-session-core with HomeActivity/HomeContext, weights bucketed per (kind, role, session) so breadth beats count, root attribution behind a RootProbe (project root, existing context, workspace marker, mount point, XDG user dir; never $HOME), an ignore list as a setting, a bounded activity tree (depth 3, 32 nodes), stages Dormant/Trace/Tile/Expanded with promotion by relevance+sessions+breadth and demotion only when later sessions AND garden-hours both pass, and a Garden Clock that advances at Lifecycle1's session edges and never on wall-clock; (2) a pure tender in lege-field (garden::tend) emitting Place/Resize/Remove with a reason each, never Move, a Place only on free cells, a Resize only when nothing but an unpinned un-user-sized garden tile yields, property-tested; (3) org.legeos.HomeGarden1 on sessiond (Observe/Tend/Contexts/Describe/Pin/Hide/Forget/ForgetAll/Clock, signal Tended) applying each tending as one HomeField1 batch, recorded in History1, with sources: the launch channel (directory arguments -> LaunchedHere with the app's role), the shell's brokered open (FileOpened), the session-edge channel (the clock); (4) the shell tends at session start and on every Home reveal edge, draws a grown Folder tile by rung (Small: name + state; Wide: + roles row of text-led tools; Large: + the branch body of used structure, heavier branches thicker, falling back to the listing), and offers place.open-* and garden.* through the one action manifest (context menu, cheat sheet, lege garden CLI). Settings shell.home-garden.* hold the levers; default on.

### Act on the Homegarden usability review: the view takes every remote change, the user's tiles are the user's, growth never shifts a neighbour, the garden verbs do what they say, a corner landing leaves room to grow

`active` · `@legeos.work.homegarden-review-fixes-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

The six findings of @legeos.assessment.homegarden-usability-review-20260908, five here and the sixth (a Settings Homegarden page) in @legeos.work.bar-cluster-clickable-20260908. (1) The shell reconciles the daemon's field on HomeField1.Changed: adopt, resize in place, remove folder tiles (field_model::reconcile_remote). (2) A folder tile the tender never placed is the user's outright: at the next tending it is pinned and kept (user_span = its span), so recession neither resizes nor removes it. (3) The tender rejects any resize whose yields shift a neighbour's cell, trying each axis alone before emitting nothing (lege-field::garden::plan_resize). (4) garden.keep is HomeGarden1.Keep (pin + freeze the size); Hide unpins and removes the tile from every Home now, undoably; Forget drops the record and removes the tile likewise; the context menu offers Pin or Unpin by the place's state and Keep only until kept. (5) A first landing takes the home corner as a 4x3 would sit in it (GROWTH_ROOM), so a Trace can become Expanded in place.

### pcmanfm-qt as the file manager: the role, the composition, and the three routes into filed

`active` · `@legeos.work.pcmanfm-qt-integration/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Make `pcmanfm-qt` the session's file manager and take `lege-files` out of the composition. `ProviderRole::FileManager` becomes a derived capability off `Categories=FileManager` (`lege-session-core/src/providers.rs`), pcmanfm-qt at priority 100; `distro/app-manifests/org.legeos.Files.json` is deleted, so nothing claims the role or `inode/directory` on Files' behalf and no shipped manifest names an uninstalled executable. `FieldAction::OpenInFiles` stops hardcoding `org.legeos.Files` and resolves the role through the providers map (`app.rs::open_in_file_manager`), reusing the "Settings ▸ Providers" sentence every unfilled role uses. Seeds swap `lege-files` for `pcmanfm-qt` plus `qt6-wayland`; the `files` component stays in `distro/deploy/components.toml` because that matrix is the build set, not the image. Integration: two DES-EMA custom actions shipped by `legeos-cli` over two new CLI subcommands (`lege home place`, `lege project create-here`), and a one-way bookmarks export from filed to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gtk-3.0/bookmarks`.

### A window that fills the screen owns the bottom edge: no tag strip, chrome on a dwell, the cluster gone, the switcher on a peek, and a tag that pins

`active` · `@legeos.work.the-bottom-edge-belongs-to-the-window-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

The user reported that a screen-filling window stops short of the bottom of the display, leaving a black row that its own tag and controls sit in, with the shell's four machine chips drawn on top of the controls; that the switcher felt like click-to-appear rather than hover-to-appear; and that clicking a name tag should pin the window and draw its name in italic. Their "full screen" is a maximized window and the black row is that window's compositor-drawn tag strip, which `client_area` subtracts from the bottom of its geometry.

One predicate carries the change: `WindowRecord::covers_screen()` = unshelved and (fullscreen or maximized), justified by the bar reserving a zone of 0 so a maximized window's work area is the whole output. `has_frame` is false for such a window, so the black row is gone; its name tag and controls are shown over it on a dwell in the bottom-right corner (`covering_chrome`, generalised from `fullscreen_chrome`); the shell's machine cluster is not drawn while one is up; and the switcher waits under it until the pointer rests on the bottom edge.

That last one needed a protocol addition. `outranks_overlay` stays fullscreen-only on purpose — promoting a maximized window over `ShellOverlay` would put the launcher, the switcher and every context menu behind the window the user is working in — so the peek could no longer be a pure stacking change: `lege_shell_manager_v1.bar_peeked` (version 7) tells the shell the edge was asked for. It enters the shell's own reveal (`BarData::peeked`) rather than bypassing `covered`, so one gesture has one way out; and the machine cluster comes back on it, so those four readings are not unreachable for as long as anything is maximized.

Three regions divide the bottom edge, each meaning one thing: the left square is Home whatever is on screen, the right square is the covering window's chrome, the band between is the peek. While that chrome is showing none of the three asks for anything — the strip is under the pointer and the strip is what is being reached for.

A click on a name tag pins the window above the others; a press that moves is the drag it always was. A pin is a sort key that borrows the `AppOnTop` slot in `stack_key` without assigning the layer, so `layer_of` still reads a pinned window as the ordinary window it is. A pinned name is drawn in a separately discovered italic face, because `pixelkit-text` has no synthetic oblique.

The strip being drawn *over* the client rather than beside it is what the whole review turned on: the gap between the tags belongs to that window rather than falling through, and a press the compositor takes is not also delivered to the client underneath.

`active` · `@legeos.work.window-manager-popup-and-functional-edge-tabs/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Rev 2 (2026-09-08, the user's decision after reading rev 1's recommendation): the reviewer's redundancy principle is kept — a window's name and controls live on the window as its tag, and the bottom edge must not repeat what has an owner — but the bar stays the pointer switcher; it is not replaced by a Windows entry and a popup. What changes is presence. The bar reserves no exclusive zone (a zero-size claim keeps it bottom-anchored). Over Home it is simply visible, full height, drawn over the garden. When a window is under its strip (any unshelved, non-fullscreen toplevel whose geometry meets the bottom BAR_HEIGHT strip while Home is not revealed) it collapses to a thin hint at the very bottom — a small ^ chevron on the bar's ground — and a pointer resting on the hint reveals the whole bar; the pointer leaving it collapses the bar again after the same short dwell, closing any open row or popover, so it hides as easily as it appears (the user's cosmic fork was slow to hide). Chip hover still opens the per-application window row after its dwell; a click on a row activates. In fullscreen nothing of the bar shows and no edge dwell reveals it: the compositor's bottom-edge peek is deleted; a visible fullscreen window stays stacked above the shell overlay on its output; Alt+Tab (MRU, campaign 4) is the switch route there. With no bottom zone a maximized window fills the output and wears its own tags (WindowService::has_frame already does this), so the bar's copies of the maximized window's controls are removed rather than kept in a shared seam; the 32px seam and the permanent Home/Windows edge entries of rev 1 are dropped. DEFERRED, not rejected: the COSMIC-derived popup window manager (Super+W, Super+secondary-click, previews) — its keyboard role is covered by Alt+Tab and its pointer-in-fullscreen role is the one open question for the trial; rev 1's popup, source-reuse and fullscreen-switching sections remain the plan for it if the trial wants a pointer route in fullscreen. ### Hands-on run in the installed session: every window resizes from all four sides, and the field draws pictures

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.four-sided-resize-and-real-icons-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Two findings from the owner's own session, both root-caused rather than patched where they showed.

Resize. lege_window::resize_edges_at answers only for a point *outside* a frame, so a frame flush with the edge of the usable area has no grabbable side there. place_new_window clamped a client's requested size to exactly the usable rectangle, and clients routinely ask for more than the screen — a size remembered from a larger monitor, a toolkit default; the compositor's own journal shows two toplevels asking for 2605x1677 and 2650x1690 on a 2560x1600 output. Clamped on the vertical axis alone that is a window which resizes from the left and the right and from neither the top nor the bottom, which is what was reported. Placement now clamps to the usable area less a resize margin on each side.

Icons. The theme search composed a fixed <size>/<context> path under three named themes. Real themes are not shaped that way — Papirus writes 48x48/apps, breeze writes apps/48, oxygen writes base/128x128/apps, today's Adwaita ships application icons only under symbolic/apps — and are not those three: this machine has no Yaru and an Adwaita with no app icons. Measured over the 206 installed .desktop entries, 82 resolved to nothing, LegeOS's own Files (system-file-manager) and Settings (preferences-system) among them, and were drawn as their first letter. The search now discovers each theme's own directories and ranks them, prefers every installed theme over none, and falls back to the -symbolic glyph last: 204 of 206. Separately the image declared no icon theme at all, so an installed LegeOS would have had nothing to find; papirus, hicolor and adwaita join the desktop layer.

### Home holds only your own things — the file manager works, running windows and the machine's instruments leave Home

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.home-purity-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

A hands-on run of the installed session on 2026-09-08 found the file manager doing nothing from Home, unselectable in Settings, and absent from the launcher under its own name; and found Home crowded with things that are not the user's own — a tile per running window, a container tile per window group, a Session, a Notifications and a Settings tile, a plate labelled "Home" standing on Home, and a permanent Help button. docs/garden/garden.md draws the line this work applies: Home deals with your stuff, the bar deals with the machine.

Four root causes, all read off the source rather than guessed. (1) The shell fetched only the `terminal` and `file-search` provider roles, so `providers[FileManager]` was never filled and every folder press took `open_in_file_manager`'s "no file manager is selected" branch on a session that had one selected. (2) The Files object's tile still launched `org.legeos.Files` by name — an application this desktop no longer ships — instead of routing through the role. (3) `derive_manifest` parsed `OnlyShowIn`/`NotShowIn` and threw them away, so `/etc/xdg/autostart/lxqt-desktop.desktop` (`OnlyShowIn=LXQt`, running `pcmanfm-qt --desktop`) won the default-variant election and the launcher's only row for PCManFM-Qt was named "Desktop" and painted a desktop. (4) The provider chooser's label was "name (import id) · priority N" in a 300px field, which elided inside the parenthesis and told the reader neither which application it was nor what its priority was.

And the subtraction: `merge_sessions` and `merge_window_groups` placed a tile for every running window and every group; `merge_system` placed the three machine widgets and `merge_panels` grouped them into a shelf. All are deleted. The merge's existing sweep removes what a saved field still carries, with no migration of its own — `wanted` never names a window tile — and one `migrate_system_tiles` takes off all seven retired system probes as ordinary invertible `Remove` ops.

### The bottom-left corner is Home, fullscreen gets the switcher back on a dwell, and the island stops sitting in the corner

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.hot-corner-fullscreen-reveal-and-a-centred-island-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Three things the user asked for on 2026-09-08 that the shell cannot do alone, because while a window owns the pointer the shell never learns where the pointer is.

1. A bottom-left hot corner reveals Home. "I would prefer a bottom left hot corner for showing the home screen, not a button" — this replaces the Home chip removed in @legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/6, whose only surviving pointer route is the Field's own context menu, which a covering window hides.

2. Fullscreen auto show/hide. "auto show/hide in full screen, and always there on the home screen itself." This reverses rev 5's deletion of the bottom-edge peek: a visible fullscreen client window sorts above the shell overlay, so the compositor has to raise the overlay on a dwell. The deleted machinery is recoverable verbatim from commit 0b6d8fc (update_bar_peek / finish_bar_peek / peek_output_at / in_peek_band, WindowService::{peek_output,set_peek_output,is_peeking}).

3. The island moves off the corner. The island now sits at the bottom-left because a zero-size zone claim anchors a surface at the start of its edge, which is exactly where the hot corner has to be — the two would fight over the same pixels. The fix is an additive alignment on the shell protocol (start / centre / end along the anchored edge) so the island can be centred the way the user's cosmic dock is, with the corner left to Home.

As built, 1 and 2 are one dwell mechanism with two intents, and the two regions are disjoint by construction rather than by a precedence rule: the corner square is Home everywhere and always (a fullscreen window included, because with no Home chip on the bar it is the only pointer route there), and the peek band is the bottom edge excluding that square. The corner is instead suppressed while a visible ShellOverlay surface is under the pointer, which makes item 3 a hard prerequisite of item 1 rather than a cosmetic improvement on it: until the shell centres its island, its collapsed 72x6 hint tab sits on top of the 8x8 corner square and the corner cannot fire.

### Install TemplarOS into the free block Windows left on the OS drive

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.install-onto-the-laptop-partitions-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Revised 2026-09-09: this record named the wrong drive. It planned --esp /dev/nvme1n1p3 --root /dev/nvme1n1p4, and nvme1n1 is the *data* drive — 875 GiB of the owner's data on p2, with a LEGEOS_ESP and a legeos-root left there by an earlier plan. The owner's intent is the opposite: never partition the data drive, and put TemplarOS on nvme0n1, the drive that carries the operating systems.

Windows has since been deleted from nvme0n1, which is what makes this straightforward. That disk now reads: a 537 GiB free block at sectors 2048..1124454399, then the 949 MiB Windows recovery partition, Lubuntu's 416 GiB root, the 100 MiB shared ESP and the 16 MiB reserved partition. The free block is at the *front*, and --free-space refused a non-tail block until it was fixed alongside this revision; planned against a sparse replica of that exact geometry it now takes the leading block, creates partitions 5 (ESP, 1 GiB, TEMPLAR_ESP) and 6 (btrfs root, the rest, templaros-root), and names all four existing partitions as kept.

Order, and every step is the owner's:
1. Back up both tables off this machine: sgdisk --backup=nvme0n1.gpt /dev/nvme0n1, and the same for nvme1n1.
2. dd the TemplarOS medium to the USB stick. Not a FAT32 copy: the image is over 4 GB. dd is uutils on this host, so no oflag=direct — it rejects an unaligned buffer with "IO error: Invalid input".
3. Boot the stick from the firmware menu with Secure Boot on. Stop on a MOK or Security Violation prompt, on casper dropping to (initramfs), or on the session not starting, and record the exact message.
4. Read the live preflight at /run/templaros/preflight.txt before anything else.
5. templaros-install --free-space /dev/nvme0n1 --user dk, read the plan, confirm it names partitions 5 and 6 and lists the four kept, then --apply.
6. Reboot without the stick and choose TemplarOS from the firmware menu; the installer appends its UEFI entry rather than making it first.

Nothing here touches nvme1n1, and Lubuntu on nvme0n1p2 stays bootable — it is the fallback until TemplarOS is trusted, and only then does the drive become wholly TemplarOS and the project move onto it.

### A partition manager on the live medium, and an installer that will not be pointed at the wrong partition

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.partition-manager-in-the-installer-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

The provisioner already refuses to be careless — --free-space creates only the two partitions it names and touches no existing one, --esp/--root formats two partitions and never writes the table, every mode prints a plan and changes nothing without --apply — but it says all of that in a terminal, in the language of device nodes. Nothing shows the owner what is on the disk before they choose, and there is no way to make the free run in the first place from inside the medium.

Two parts, both reusing what exists rather than writing a partitioner:

1. gparted joins the live layer in distro/seeds/selection.toml (live medium only; the installed system gets none of it), and `legeos-install --partition` launches it, waits, then re-reads the table with partprobe and re-plans. GParted is the partition editor a person may already know, it is the one that will not let a mounted filesystem be moved, and writing another one is the mistake this is meant to prevent.

2. `legeos-install` grows a disk step it prints before anything else: every partition on the target device with its size, type, filesystem, label and — if it is mounted or holds a mounted filesystem — where; the largest free run; and which two partitions the plan would use, named. It refuses, rather than warns, on a partition that is mounted, that is the ESP the live medium itself booted from, or that holds the running system.

The hazard this exists for is concrete on the reference laptop: /dev/nvme1n1p4 is the intended LegeOS root and is at this moment mounted as the ISO build volume, holding the archive and a 4 GB ISO. An installer that formats what it was pointed at would take the medium being installed from with it.

### The island floats: an Argb8888 buffer on the bar's surface, its alpha from a coverage mask, with the opaque present as the fallback

The user asked for "a collection of icons floating", not a bar. The island is content-width since this morning, but it is still an opaque square plate: the bar is a winit window over softbuffer, which attaches an `Xrgb8888` buffer, so every pixel the frame does not write is black and nothing can be rounded or gapped.

### Home Field — taskbar-free desktop surface: tiles, parked sessions, go-home, information row, projects and previews

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-field/2` · part of `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1`

Replace the drawer-list Home Surface with the Home Field: a bounded, taskbar-free field of rectangular tiles (projects, active apps / parked sessions, file trays, widgets, system) on the shell's Layer::HomeSurface backdrop. Installed-but-idle desktop entries remain searchable instead of automatically covering the field. Windows collapse into tiles instead of minimising and expand back out; a bare Super tap is the primary temporary Home toggle, with Ctrl+Alt+H and Super+D retained as fallbacks, and the reveal changes no window state. A standard information row on Home begins with local date/time, live/parked counts, and the selected network-status provider, using nm-tray2 for network control. Dragging a tile onto a target performs a typed, previewed, undoable operation; layout is a stable local grid that never reflows globally, persisted per output by sessiond (org.legeos.HomeField1). Phases: 1 compositor truths (shelved windows actually hidden and not hit-tested, maximize, reveal-home command + keybindings + protocol v2 with identifier/geometry), 2 the pure crates/lege-field model (document, ops with inverses, local reflow, representation ladder, drag/throw state machine), 3 FieldScreen in lege-shell with --print field and full keyboard reach, 4 HomeField1 persistence, 5 projects/trays/zoom, 6 previews over ext-image-copy-capture, 7 lege-treemap and budgeted widgets, 8 the throw spike with a keep/delete rule. Plan of record: ~/.claude/plans/for-this-project-i-crispy-shannon.md (author's machine).

### Home Field widget foundations — neighbour-yielding resize, the widget contract, the action manifest, and Lifecycle1 as the service pattern

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-widget-foundations/3` · part of `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1`

The Home Field was a dead end for a desktop tester: no way to launch anything, no logout/restart/shutdown, no way to close a window, and a search bar that does nothing outside an expanded drawer. The decision is that every missing capability arrives as a widget on the one screen rather than as a panel or tray, consistent with M2's taskbar-free commitment. This item builds only the foundation those widgets stand on, in four parts. (1) A resize that lets adjacent tiles give up span instead of being evicted: reflow::find_resize, where a yielding neighbour keeps its far edge and the request is clamped to the largest span every neighbour can absorb. (2) The widget contract over TileKind::System, which was a designed-for slot nothing constructed: a descriptor declares what shows at each representation rung and which regions are clickable, and each region names an action rather than coding a behaviour. (3) An action manifest in lege-types, so one declaration drives the shell's labels, the keyboard accelerator and the lege verb. (4) org.legeos.Session.Lifecycle1 on sessiond forwarding to logind, built as the one worked example of the service-interface pattern every future widget follows.

### Home Field widgets — every missing desktop capability as a tile on the one screen

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1` · part of `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1`

A gap review of the Home Field against what any desktop of the last twenty years offers found that a cold session gives the user eight drawer tiles and the message "open an application and it will appear", with no way to open one. Application tiles are derived only from windows that are already running and are removed when the last one closes, so the launcher route is circular. There is no logout, restart, shutdown, suspend or lock; no way to close a window; no volume, brightness or battery; no notification rendering despite sessiond hosting the notification server; no context menus; and the field's own search bar does nothing outside an expanded drawer. The decision is that each of these arrives as a widget on the single screen — information first, sub-clickable, opening a window only as a deliberate second step — rather than as a panel, a dock or a tray, which is consistent with M2's taskbar-free commitment and with homefield.md's rule that the launcher is inventory and the home screen is working memory. @legeos.work.home-widget-foundations built the framework; this item is the umbrella for the widgets themselves and for the window controls that are still missing.

## [Lane B — shell: the persistent bottom bar with indicators, the taskbar with its hover row, and the maximized window's controls](ACTIVE-WORK.md#lane-b--shell-the-persistent-bottom-bar-with-indicators-the-taskbar-with-its-hover-row-and-the-maximized-windows-controls) `@legeos.work.bottom-bar-taskbar/7`

### The hover row's two remaining gaps against the cosmic-applets fork: a header naming what is being switched, and a shorter dwell when a row is already open

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.bar-hover-row-switcher-header-20260908/1` · part of `@legeos.work.bottom-bar-taskbar/7`

Two things the user's own cosmic-applets fork (branch local/dock-window-grouping) has and LegeOS's hover row still does not, neither built in the previews pass.

1. A header on the row. The fork's window_switcher_view (cosmic-app-list/src/app.rs:914) puts the application's icon, its name and its window count above the tiles. LegeOS's row is tiles alone: it opens under the chip you are pointing at, so the application is implied — but it opens 104 pixels above the bar, over whatever window is there, and at that distance from its chip the implication weakens. Worth having; costs a band and one more opaque shape to record (the ARGB surface shows nothing that is not in BarScreen::opaque).

2. A shorter dwell when a row is already open. The fork has two: HOVER_OPEN_DELAY_MS 225 to open the first switcher, HOVER_SWITCH_DELAY_MS 80 to move to another icon once one is up (app.rs:587-592). LegeOS has one, HOVER_OPEN_MS 400 (bar_screen.rs:167), so walking the chips with a row open costs the full dwell at every chip and the row flickers shut between them. This is the cheaper of the two and the more felt: one constant and one branch in BarScreen::update_hover, where the branch already knows whether a row is open.

Deliberately not in this list: the fork's per-tile close button (see the note on BarAction::Window below), its New Window button, and its hover_previews config gate. The close button is nearly wired — BarAction::Window { id, window } exists in bar_screen.rs and app.rs:2583 already performs it, and no code path produces one — so it is a design question (is a second route to a control the window already wears on its own tag wanted?) rather than an implementation one, and it is the user's to answer. New Window duplicates Home, which is this desktop's launcher. The config gate is a second setting for one hover row when HomeFieldSettings::previews already turns the pictures off.

## [Integrated design roadmap — Home, Files, perimeter resize, event services and Developer Edition storage](ACTIVE-WORK.md#integrated-design-roadmap--home-files-perimeter-resize-event-services-and-developer-edition-storage) `@legeos.work.design-consolidation-roadmap/1`

### WS6 — build identity, local archive, lege dev deploy, compatibility gates, and replay-gated resourced improvements

`active` · `@legeos.work.deployment-activation-and-resourced/1` · part of `@legeos.work.design-consolidation-roadmap/1`

Tracks A-E, landing order A1 A2 A3 A4 B1 B2 B3 E0 C1 C2 B4 E1 E5 E6 D1 D2 E2 E3 E4 C3. Track A: BuildSetId is the Debian version (0.1.0~dev<epoch>+g<sha7>[.dirty]) across all 13 packages via cargo xtask build-set, which rejects mixed sets; every long-lived process writes a runtime build stamp file at startup (filesystem-first because comp and shell serve no D-Bus; not RuntimeDirectory=, which would delete siblings' stamps); distro/deploy/components.toml is the machine-readable component matrix; lege dev status computes installed-versus-running convergence; doctor gains BuildSetCoherent and RunningMatchesInstalled with PackageAgesConsistent as the documented fallback. Track B: a local signed APT repo at /var/lib/legeos/devrepo (apt-ftparchive + per-developer gpg key, keep=3 sets), one transactional apt-get install --allow-downgrades per set, lege dev rollback as the same path, and an activation engine with per-component rules — shell restart with health gate, apps at next launch, resourced controlled restart, sessiond/filed/portal only when the compatibility gates pass (shipped manual until the composed-session restart test exists), hostd blocked mid-transaction, compositor always needs-session, kernel/boot needs-reboot — ending in the convergence report with the previous set retained. Track C: xtask interface-baseline/check-interface-signatures turns the frozen-signature convention into an enforced gate; lege-state gains schema_meta with min_reader_version, an open()-time refusal of too-new databases, VACUUM INTO snapshots, and the documented one-rollback-generation policy; lege-field gains a document migration registry applied at the load boundary with DocumentTooNew never overwriting. Track D: lege-boot-health calls MarkGood/Rollback itself, and hostd's reconcile_boot wires the GRUB tries counter; cryptographic verification and the hardware matrix stay explicitly deferred. Track E, all gated behind the E0 replay harness (replay recorded traces through Governor::decide with a round-trip fidelity test): thresholds scale with MemTotal (reserve clamp 6.25% 768MiB-4GiB, critical clamp 2% 256MiB-1.5GiB, reproducing today's constants at 48GiB), unsaved-work gains a producer and a TTL via additive SetInstanceWork, richer safe-to-sacrifice signals via additive SetInstanceActivity (idle age, project importance, checkpoint freshness reaching scoring for the first time, user pin as strong weight never hard exclusion), Governor::plan returns multi-step reclaim plans (Elevated trims up to three, Severe throttles top-K to the deficit, Critical stays single-victim) with the foreground structurally excluded at Severe unless demonstrably the runaway, protect.rs stops lowering memory.low and covers sessiond and filed, and ADR-0014 settles systemd-oomd ownership (armed backstop on app.slice at 90%, off on session.slice, avoid on the five session units).

### Next Home usability sequence — adaptable Home, complete folder surfaces, then common Settings

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1` · part of `@legeos.work.home-field/2`

Carry the Home surface from a fixed demonstration layout to an ordinary daily desktop in the order set by the user on 2026-08-31.

First, make Home itself adaptable: configurable Home-only panels/rails/docks, automatic panel layouts for different output shapes, user-invoked arrangements for all open windows, and immediate reversible switching among those arrangements. Preserve truly chrome-free fullscreen application work and refine bare Super from release-only toggling into immediate press/hold Home reveal with shortcut-safe semantics.

Second, make folders and composite shortcut panes the Home file objects. Build copy/cut/paste, drag and drop, delete/trash and the remaining ordinary file verbs on the multi-selection foundation; then add deterministic sorting and list-versus-thumbnail presentation. Loose individual file tiles are explicitly not part of this model.

Third, make the graphical Settings app adjust the common controls a person expects: resolution/refresh/rotation/scale, mouse and trackpad behaviour, and appearance/theme/material choices. Accessibility remains deferred behind these product-completeness items per the user's standing priority.

### Interim application integration — the Terminal role and the Super+grave drop-down terminal, the Files context menu, the search panel with FSearch as the FileSearch provider, Kitty defaults

`active` · `@legeos.work.application-integration-interim/2` · part of `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1`

Integration choices the user made on 2026-09-03, revised later the same day. (a) Terminal: ProviderRole::Terminal, exclusive, candidates from TerminalEmulator desktop entries, default kitty; the shell relays the selection with lege_shell_manager_v1.set_terminal and answers terminal_requested by launching the provider through the launch chain; Super+grave (compositor chord; a bare ~ or ` is a typed character and cannot be a global chord) toggles the terminal: launch when none, unshelve/activate when shelved or unfocused, shelve and refocus the previous window when focused, never close. No Ctrl+Alt+T. 'Open terminal here' in the Files context menu launches it with --directory. /etc/xdg/kitty/kitty.conf shipped by legeos-shell with the LegeOS palette, background_opacity 0.85, remember_window_size no, wayland_titlebar_color system, overridable by ~/.config/kitty. (b) Files object: secondary-click menu on rows and empty space reusing surface/context_menu.rs and the declared files.* verbs (Open, Open with…, Open terminal here, Copy path, Rename, Move to trash, Properties; New folder, Paste, Select all, Sort by…, Show hidden), then multi-select, keyboard verbs, drag-and-drop and properties-as-pane. (c) Search: the top field on Home stays the application launcher only (COSMIC's launcher shape); real search is the Files object's search field expanded into a partial-screen panel (about two thirds of the field, centred, hairline edge) over lege-filed's scoped index with path, size and modified time per row and keyboard navigation, whose last row is 'Search everywhere with FSearch'; ProviderRole::FileSearch, exclusive, launched with --search <query>; 'Search here…' in the context menu. The later indexing direction replaces the interim two-database arrangement: lege-filed owns one persistent, incrementally maintained derived file index used by integrated Files search, a remote-index FSearch fork, Silvaview-rs, the CLI and future clients.

### Act on the second hands-on run: adjustable windows, visible tiling, body-drag tiles, concise labels, a route to drives, one Settings widget

`active` · `@legeos.work.hands-on-run-2-fixes/2` · part of `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1` · **at risk**

Fix every deficiency in @legeos.observation.hands-on-run-20260831-findings. (1) Windows are adjustable: the compositor's recovery-band move and corner-grip resize actually start their grabs (they previously demanded an implicit grab that cannot exist yet at band-press time, so both affordances were dead on real hardware). (2) New windows are placed — centred in the usable area, cascaded, size-clamped — instead of honouring a meaningless (0,0) request flush into the corner. (3) Arranging from the Home menu ends the reveal so the result is visible, and arranging with no windows open says so on the field. (4) Object-like tiles (file, folder, pane, app) drag-move from anywhere in their body; instrument tiles keep the band. (5) Browse rows and grids drop the FOLDER/FILE caption noise: the name leads, '/' marks a folder, extensions name files once, folders read as the folder material. (6) The browse toolbar's path is a clickable breadcrumb and a Files button hands the folder to org.legeos.Files with its drives sidebar. (7) The battery/volume/brightness widgets consolidate into ONE Settings widget whose click opens the Settings app, per the user's direct instruction.

### Graphical Settings for displays, mouse/trackpad and Home appearance

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-field-settings-gui/1` · part of `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1`

The graphical Settings app already edits the five Home Field tuning keys; replace the vague goal of making every read-only diagnostic tab editable with the common controls needed for daily use.

Displays: enumerate connected outputs and allow resolution, refresh rate, rotation/orientation and scale per output, including mixed-scale arrangements. Apply through compositor-owned validated configuration with a visible confirmation countdown and automatic rollback when the new mode is not confirmed or the output disappears. Show the resulting logical arrangement before applying and retain a known-good configuration.

Mouse and trackpad: expose pointer speed, acceleration profile, natural scrolling, primary-button choice and scroll behaviour; for touchpads also tap-to-click, tap-and-drag, two-finger/edge scrolling and disable-while-typing where libinput supports them. Unsupported controls are identified as unavailable rather than drawn as inert switches.

Appearance: select light/dark or bundled themes, accent and object-material palette/texture roles, background/wallpaper behaviour, and the defaults used by Home panels, folder panes and widgets. Themes are declarative design tokens/material assets, never executable shell extensions, and application fullscreen remains free of Home chrome. Every graphical setting writes through a typed service/schema and has Reset; CLI inspection/change remains equivalent. Provider, association, history and hardware diagnostic pages may remain read-only until their own scoped work exists.

### Lane A — compositor: bottom tags replace the title band, the corner grip goes, a maximized window under the bar has no frame

`active` · `@legeos.work.window-tags-replace-the-band/3` · part of `@legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next/1`

lege-window: RECOVERY_BAND_HEIGHT becomes TAG_HEIGHT and recovery_band becomes tag_strip, the full-width strip at a window's bottom edge; client_area/frame_around keep the origin and differ by one strip height; repair_window clamps so the bottom strip stays on an output (a tall window hangs off the top); move_into_view sets a too-tall window flush with the bottom edge; resize_grip and RESIZE_GRIP_SIZE are deleted and MIN_WINDOW_HEIGHT is two tag heights; Output::reserves_bottom derives 'a bar holds this edge' from the usable area; WindowService::has_frame is false for fullscreen and for a maximized window on an output that reserves its bottom, so the shell's bar carries those controls and the compositor draws the tags again when no zone is claimed. Compositor chrome: layout::control_tags/control_tag_at (the former band_buttons, verbatim) and layout::name_tag (left end, up to TAG_GAP before the first control, capped at NAME_TAG_MAX_WIDTH); collect_name_tag and collect_control_tags replace collect_band and collect_grip and bail when !has_frame. Input: Affordance::Tag replaces Band, Grip is gone, the gap between the tags falls through to the window beneath, edges and corners resize as before. window_groups::tag_drop_target hit-tests the name tag only. COMPOSITOR.md's band rows describe tags. Also: on_outputs_changed's repairs now configure every repaired window through space_sync::apply_resized_geometry, not X11 alone, so a maximized Wayland client is re-sent its size when the bar appears.

## [Home Field widgets — every missing desktop capability as a tile on the one screen](ACTIVE-WORK.md#home-field-widgets--every-missing-desktop-capability-as-a-tile-on-the-one-screen) `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1`

### Launcher widget — make a cold session able to open its first application

`active` · `@legeos.work.home-widget-launcher/2` · part of `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1`

A launcher widget that lists installed applications, filters as the user types, and launches through Launcher1. This is the single most load-bearing gap: without it a freshly booted session cannot open anything at all, because application tiles are derived from windows that already exist (field_model::merge_apps) and are removed when the last one closes. The inventory is already in the shell — AppIdentity1.ListApps is fetched every three seconds into ShellApp::apps and its only consumer today is a grep for nm-tray — and Launcher1.Launch already works and is already called for the network control and for opening files. The widget itself is small; the prerequisites below are not.

### Drive the compositor's ext-session-lock-v1 so Lifecycle1.Lock stops returning NotSupported

`active` · `@legeos.work.session-lock-client/1` · part of `@legeos.work.home-widgets/1`

Make locking the session actually lock it. The compositor implements ext-session-lock-v1 in full (compositor/lege-comp/src/session_lock.rs) and ADR-0010 makes the lock screen compositor-owned, "one provider by construction". What has never existed is anything that drives it: no client calls lock(), so there is no lock surface and no lock. Lifecycle1.Lock is declared with the interface shape settled and returns NotSupported rather than reporting a success it did not achieve.

## [Memory governor, watcher host and file-index effectiveness — the Astra-ranked fix set](ACTIVE-WORK.md#memory-governor-watcher-host-and-file-index-effectiveness--the-astra-ranked-fix-set) `@legeos.work.memory-polling-indexing-effectiveness-20260909/1`

### Deferred — the btrfs delta backend seeds its own baseline, commits the pointer only after apply, rearms watches after catch-up, and bounds the stream read

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.btrfs-delta-baseline-checkpoint-protocol-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.work.memory-polling-indexing-effectiveness-20260909/1` · **at risk**

services/lege-filed/src/delta_catchup.rs (~145-156) returns without a baseline when none exists, and ensure_baseline has no production caller, so a fresh opt-in never seeds itself; plant (~236-247) writes the baseline pointer before decode and apply have succeeded, and the existing tests never inspect that file; a successful catch-up skips recursive watch rearming; crates/lege-file-index/src/btrfs_delta.rs (~320-325) reads the send stream with an unbounded read_to_end although the host checks reported bytes. Design one atomic applied-index/baseline checkpoint (pointer written in the same commit as the applied generation, or after it with a recovery rule) and a watch-coverage step after catch-up, then implement. The reader byte limit is independent and may land ahead of the redesign.

### Deferred — Index::children by an indexed parent lookup, once parent_id is correct on every path and the read views have a contract

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.index-children-parent-id-contract-20260909/1` · part of `@legeos.work.memory-polling-indexing-effectiveness-20260909/1` · **at risk**

crates/lege-file-index/src/lib.rs Index::children (~575-598) retrieves and decodes the whole descendant range and filters immediate children in Rust, so recursive reconciliation pays for every descendant at every level. An indexed parent lookup needs parent_id correctness first: take-on-trust reconciliation observes directories with parent None, and mutation::place_at does not update parent_id on a move. Search/query reads and cursor row materialisation also use distinct live views. Write the contract (parent_id is set on every committed entry; a query and its cursor materialise from one view), fix the two writers, measure the reconcile workload against @legeos.observation.reconciliation-cost-tracks-tree-size-not-change-size, then switch children to the indexed lookup.

**Acceptance** — 0 of 2 satisfied

| `parent-id-invariant` | command | not satisfied — no evidence |

## Unparented

### Nine acceptance and evidence commands name a test filter that matches nothing

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.acceptance-checks-that-cannot-fail/1`

CORRECTED 2026-09-08, after the first version of this record over-counted. `cargo test`'s
filter is a SUBSTRING match against the full test path, `crate::module::test_name`, so a filter
naming a module — `keybindings::tests`, or a bare module name — is live even though that exact
string appears nowhere in any file's text: the source has `mod keybindings;` in one place and
`mod tests` in another, and the module name may only ever appear as a FILE NAME. A literal
content grep calls those phantom and is wrong. The first version of this record listed eleven;
`consumer_contract` and `migration_0006` are real module files (`git ls-files` matches the
path, not the content) and `override_dh_auto_configure` is a real target in debian/rules. The
corrected scan matches a token against tracked file PATHS as well as tracked file CONTENT, and
excludes .akr/ and docs/generated/ so the ledger cannot vouch for itself.

THE MECHANISM IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE POINT. `cargo test -p <crate> <filter>` exits 0 when the
filter matches no test — it prints "running 0 tests ... test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; N
filtered out" — so a `command` gate naming a test that no longer exists is satisfied without
executing anything. It is a gate that cannot fail, and nothing in the ledger can tell it apart
from one that passed.

THE CORRECTED FINDING. Of 299 command slots on live records at e6e1b1c3, carrying 104 distinct
filter tokens, nine match nothing in the tracked source by path or by content:

- `the_switcher_hides_under_a_window_that_fills_the_screen_and_comes_back_on_a_peek` on
  @legeos.work.the-bottom-edge-belongs-to-the-window-20260908 — FIXED during this pass; the real
  test is `the_switcher_hides_only_under_a_window_that_fills_the_screen`
  (shell/lege-shell/src/surface/app.rs:4765), which covers both halves.
- `band_buttons_pack_against_the_right_edge_close_last` and
  `a_narrow_band_keeps_close_and_gives_up_the_rest` — @legeos.evidence.hands-on-3-band-controls-20260903
  (verified) and @legeos.work.hands-on-run-3-fixes (active).
- `the_client_area_sits_under_the_band` and `edges_are_grabbed_just_outside_the_frame` —
  @legeos.evidence.hands-on-3-frame-geometry-20260903 (verified) and
  @legeos.work.hands-on-run-3-fixes (active).
- `the_field_paints_nothing_in_the_bar_strip` — @legeos.evidence.field-stays-above-the-bar-strip-20260907
  (verified).
- `wanted_size_is_the_chips_alone_until_a_row_or_controls_need_the_width` —
  @legeos.work.bottom-bar-taskbar (active).
- `input_settings` and `display_configuration` — @legeos.work.home-field-settings-gui (active).

STATE CHANGES WHAT EACH ONE MEANS, and it is worth separating them rather than counting to nine.
None sits on a `completed` record, so nothing in this ledger was completed against a gate that
executed nothing. Four sit on `active` work, where a filter naming a test that does not exist
YET is a specification rather than a false gate — home-field-settings-gui has not been built.
The ones that matter are the four on `verified` evidence recording `result pass`: those are
assertions in the ledger's own voice about work that was reviewed and closed. They are not
lying — a command ran and exited 0 — but what they attest to is nothing. The four belong to the
band and frame-geometry design that the later covers_screen work replaced, which is why the
honest repair for them is probably to retire the checks rather than rename them.

WHAT THE NEXT SESSION MUST DECIDE. For each of the four `verified` evidence records: re-run
against the correct test and revise, or supersede as vacuous. Leaving them is the one option
that keeps a claim in the ledger that no one can check. For the four on `active` work, nothing
is needed until completion, but completion must not close them as they stand.

THE GENERAL FIX, and the constraint on it that is not obvious: a sweep comparing every
acceptance and evidence command's filter tokens against the tracked source belongs in
`just check` — but it MUST match the way cargo does, as a substring against the full test path,
checking file paths as well as file contents. A literal name lookup reproduces the exact
false-positive class described at the top of this record: on this ledger it would have flagged
eight healthy gates alongside the nine real ones.

### Ubuntu-derived full distribution and latest-stable kernel roadmap

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.full-distribution-roadmap/1`

Turn the LegeOS desktop/session and existing distro scaffold into a supportable amd64 Ubuntu 26.04
binary derivative: clean source builds, signed overlay archive, reproducible image and live installer,
safe in-series updates, recovery, security operations, hardware qualification, and a LegeOS-owned
latest-qualified-stable kernel lane. Linux release candidates remain experimental and Ubuntu's signed
GA kernel remains a rescue path until the independent kernel/driver/signing pipeline is proven.

### Nothing on this machine stops one process taking all of it, and the session survives just enough to be useless

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.no-memory-ceiling-on-developer-tooling/1`

Close the gap @legeos.observation.one-developer-tool-froze-the-machine-for-45-minutes-20260908
measured: a single rust-analyzer at 19.9 GB RSS exhausted 31 GB of memory and 7.8 GiB of swap,
the load average reached 57.89, no OOM killer fired, no cgroup constrained anything, and the
compositor and shell both stayed alive and unresponsive for 45 minutes. Killing one process
fixed it instantly. LegeOS is meant to be a machine a developer can work on and build the
system itself on, so a build tool being able to do this to it is a distro-level defect and not
a user error.

NOT DESIGNED HERE. This record exists so the incident is not lost and so the choice is made
deliberately by the user rather than by whoever hits it next. Four levers are on the table and
they are not alternatives so much as layers:

(1) A memory ceiling on developer tooling. systemd slices already exist and LegeOS already
writes unit files: a dev-tools.slice with MemoryMax and MemoryHigh would have capped the
indexer at a number the user chose, and the tool would have been reclaimed or killed instead of
the machine. Cheapest and most targeted, and it fits the existing session/units layout.

(2) A userspace pressure daemon. The kernel OOM killer did not fire, which is the normal and
much-documented behaviour when a machine is thrashing rather than allocating: it is making
progress, very slowly, so nothing declares an emergency. earlyoom, systemd-oomd or nohang act
on PSI pressure instead of on allocation failure, which is exactly the signal this incident
produced.

(3) zram in place of, or in front of, a swap partition. Seven point eight gigabytes of disk
swap is what turned an out-of-memory condition into forty-five minutes of page faults. A
compressed in-memory swap fails faster and more honestly, which on a laptop is the better
failure.

(4) A route out from inside the session. The compositor stayed alive, which is the good news
and the bad news: the user could see their desktop and could do nothing with it. Whatever else
is decided, lege-comp should reserve a way to reach a process list and kill something under
memory pressure — a compositor-owned chord that does not depend on the shell, the way the lock
screen is compositor-owned rather than client-owned.

WHAT THE NEXT SESSION MUST DECIDE, in this order: whether (1) alone is enough for the reference
machine, or whether (2) is wanted as the general answer for a distro that will run on hardware
with less memory than this one; whether (3) changes the installer's storage plan, since
@legeos.decision.independent-storage-roles and the provisioner currently lay out a swap
partition; and whether (4) is in scope for Developer Edition 0.1 or belongs after it. Only (4)
touches the compositor; (1) and (3) touch the installer and the unit files; (2) is a package
selection and a policy.

One measurement worth taking before deciding anything: what the same indexing run costs under
a MemoryMax that is generous but finite. If it completes, (1) is the whole answer for this
machine and the rest is for other hardware.

### pixelkit should carry alpha, so a shell surface can be a shape without painting it twice

`proposed` · `@legeos.work.pixelkit-should-carry-alpha-so-a-surface-can-be-a-shape/1`

Upstream work in the sibling `pixelkit` repository (`../pixelkit`, which has its own `.akr`), recorded here because LegeOS is the consumer that needs it and is currently paying for its absence.

`pixelkit_raster::WindowBuffer` is `Vec<u32>` holding `0x00RRGGBB`, and `Painter::blend` takes alpha as a *weight* — `blend_channels(destination, source, alpha)` mixes colour channels and stores nothing in the top byte. There is no way to ask the painter what a pixel's coverage was, so a surface that wants to be a shape rather than a rectangle cannot get its alpha channel out of the toolkit that drew it.

What LegeOS does instead, today: it renders the shape a second time, white on black, through the same `fill_rounded_rect_aa` primitive, and reads the low byte of that second buffer as coverage (`ShellApp::redraw_bar`, `BarScreen::opaque_shapes`, `ShmBuffer::write_masked`). It works and it is anti-aliased, but it is two rasterisations for one frame, it obliges every drawing surface to declare its solid shapes separately from painting them, and the two can drift apart — the comment on `opaque` says as much.

What is wanted upstream: an alpha channel the painter maintains. Either `WindowBuffer` becomes premultiplied `0xAARRGGBB` throughout with `blend_channels` composing coverage rather than discarding it, or a `CoverageBuffer` is written alongside the colour one by the same primitives. The first is the honest one and the larger change; the second is closer to what LegeOS hand-rolls now and would let it delete the second pass without changing pixelkit's colour semantics.

**Acceptance** — 0 of 2 satisfied

| Check | Method | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no-visual-change` | manual | not satisfied — no evidence |
| `one-rasterisation` | command | not satisfied — no evidence |
